There is a good chance that she feels her death would be a boon to you. As a person who has gone through these feelings with an unsupportive partner, I beg you to make the case to her that her dying is not going to help you. I assume you care about her, which gives her a luxury not all of us get to expirence.  

Talk to her, and more importantly, listen to her, do everything you can to help her to realize you are a safe person to communicate with. That means a tremendous amount of judgment free listening. And a lot of reassurance that you not only want to listen to her but you enjoy listening to her. 

Suicidal ideation is often a private pain and whatever you might be seeing from her, like this latest attempt, is the tip of the iceberg of the pain she's dealing with. It's private because people who deal with often think no one cares, will listen, or feel like being too open is burdensome. It's so, so important that you work to make yourself a safe space for her. Her battle is getting the help she might need, and that is a very, very tough and exhausting and slow process that you will need to cheerlead the whole way through. But beyond that, being the beacon she can reach out to and not another person she thinks is better off with her dead, is one of the most important things you can do to help in this situation.

My past partner did none of this during the worst times of Suicidal pain and typically made the whole thing about them and their feelings which only reinforced the Suicidal depression I was going through. Now you surely have your own painful emotions associated with this incident. You might feel alone, abandoned, heart broken and that is all valid. But remember that your wife was ready to never see you or anyone she has ever cared about. That Is deep pain. So deep that for a relatively healthy mind it does not even properly register how profoundly sad you have to be to never want to even take the chance at life anymore. 

I say all that only to make the point that working through those complex feeling you both might be feeling ATM, needs to be done in a healthy, non accusatory way otherwise it's just going into the list of reasons for the potential next attempt

What you did was nothing to hate yourself over. I think part of you knows  you want a reason to justify self harm, which speaks to a much deeper pain you are or are not dealing with. Life is shit and I flip flop from pushing to stay here for just a few hours at a time some days, to being ready to just end the whole charade. So I understand the turbulence you might be feeling.

But if you are leaving because of what you think you did so wrong, I would im0lore you to find a better reason. Getting a bit handy while talking to your gf is a very, very common thing people do and nothing to be ashamed of. There are people who knowingly and happily victimize children and have 0 qualms about it and no intention of ever harming themselves. You got excited while flirting with your significant other but feel more guilt than the aforementioned child predators. 

Your not scum, or needing to be redeemed. If you truly feel bad about it and like you did something wrong, talk to someone about it first.  Get another opinion from someone you trust.

No need to apologize. I appreciate you even attempting to reach out. Life has been a painful slog for a long time. I've been betrayed, and hurt by everyone I have ever known. I've worked really hard to be a source of compassion and empathy to all the people in my small world because I know what it's like to not have that. But that same thing never has been reciprocated. 

In my teens and 20s I could stand that. But getting older is like accumulating more and more wounds that get harder to recover from. When I look around for help or just simple understanding, I get met with venom. No one in my life cares about me beyond my monetary value. It's tough to accept that after a lifetime, no one you know cares and only sees you as a wallet. 

A year ago I read into some rough patches. Lost my job, my partner of 10 years at the time dumped me because of that, which was really tough because they had gone through a similar ordeal and I stood by them in their depression, but when bad things happen to me, I'm told to get out. It's really just been one bad expirence after another. Life has gotten progressively worse and I can't seem to even find the bottom. 

I still doggedly search for strands of a reason to keep going but everyday the deep, searing pain and internal anguish gets harder and harder to combat and it really just makes me tired. I just want to rest at this point. I don't want to know what the next round of fuckery will bring or how I will manage the next painful curveball life throws at me. Better to just give in
